conceptBreakdown.content:
Oxygen is transported in blood in two forms:
1. **Dissolved in Plasma ($3\%$)**: Due to poor water solubility.
2. **Bound to Hemoglobin ($97\%$)**: As Oxyhemoglobin ($\text{Hb}_4(\text{O}_2)_4$) inside erythrocytes.

### Hemoglobin Architecture & Delivery
- Tetramer ($\text{MW} \approx 64,500\text{ Da}$) of two $\alpha$ and two $\beta$ globin chains ($\alpha_2\beta_2$), each containing a heme group with central $\text{Fe}^{2+}$.
- $1\text{ g of Hb}$ binds up to $1.34\text{ mL of }\text{O}_2$. At $15\text{ g Hb/100 mL}$, oxygen capacity is $\approx 20\text{ mL }\text{O}_2 / 100\text{ mL blood}$.
- Under resting conditions, $100\text{ mL}$ of blood delivers $\approx 5\text{ mL of }\text{O}_2$ to tissues ($25\%$ extraction ratio).

### 6.1 The Oxygen-Hemoglobin Dissociation Curve & The Bohr Effect
- **$P_{50}$ Parameter**: Partial pressure of $\text{O}_2$ at which Hb is $50\%$ saturated ($P_{50} \approx 26.6\text{ mmHg}$).
- **The Bohr Effect (Right Shift / $\text{O}_2$ Unloading at Tissues)**: High $p\text{CO}_2$, high $\text{H}^+$ (low $\text{pH}$), high temperature, and elevated $2,3\text{-BPG}$ stabilize deoxyhemoglobin in its T-state, shifting curve to the RIGHT and releasing $\text{O}_2$.
- **Left Shift (Alveolar $\text{O}_2$ Loading)**: High $p\text{O}_2$, low $p\text{CO}_2$, low $\text{H}^+$ (higher $\text{pH}$), and cool temperatures stabilize the R-state, promoting $\text{O}_2$ binding.
- **Fetal Hemoglobin ($\text{HbF}, \alpha_2\gamma_2$)**: Binds $2,3\text{-BPG}$ poorly, exhibiting a significantly higher affinity for $\text{O}_2$ than adult $\text{HbA}$ (curve shifted LEFT).
